candidates.title: Alleviating cosmological strong coupling with torsion in regularized 4D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The four-dimensional scalar-tensor theory obtained by conformally regularizing the Gauss-Bonnet term has a vanishing kinetic term for the scalar perturbation mode on its late-time de Sitter attractor, signaling strong coupling. We show that, when the regularization is carried out in Riemann-Cartan geometry, the resulting theory admits de Sitter attractors with trace torsion on which this kinetic term remains nonvanishing. On spatially flat FLRW backgrounds with trace torsion, the quadratic actions for perturbations describe one scalar mode and two tensor modes, while the vector perturbations are nondynamical. We identify a nonempty parameter region admitting de Sitter attractors whose scalar and tensor perturbations are free of ghost and gradient instabilities at all momenta.
candidates.authors: Jianhui Qiu, Ling-Wei Luo, Chunhui Liu, Chao-Qiang Geng

candidates.title: Timelike entanglement entropy with gravitational anomaly from complexified geometry
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) in a two-dimensional conformal field theory with a gravitational anomaly, $c_L\neq c_R$, dual to topologically massive gravity in AdS$_3$. Holographically, the TEE is determined by the on-shell action of a massive spinning particle on a single complex geodesic anchored at the endpoints of the timelike interval. This action consists of the complex geodesic length and the twist of a parallel-transported normal frame. We carry out the computation in Poincar\'e AdS$_3$, non-extremal and extremal rotating BTZ backgrounds, and provide an equivalent Chern-Simons derivation in which the bulk connection stays real while only the saddle of the Wilson-line probe becomes complex. In each case, the holographic result matches the corresponding TEE in dual field theory. The real part of the TEE is fixed unambiguously whereas its imaginary part depends on the boundary $i\epsilon$ prescription and the orientation of the interval. In the bulk, the dependence on orientation reflects an ambiguity in the choice of framing. Along the complex geodesic, the residual frame group becomes $SO(2,\mathbb C)\simeq\mathbb C^*$, so the endpoint conditions determine the frame twist only up to integer multiples of $2\pi i$. The difference between the two orientations, $\frac{c_L-c_R}{6}\,i\pi$, is fixed entirely by the gravitational anomaly and persists for the R\'enyi pseudo-entropies.
candidates.authors: Minwoo Lim, Himanshu Parihar, Junggi Yoon

candidates.title: The metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron: parameter-free inflation
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a model of slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity, where the connection is independent of the metric. We require that the Einstein-Hilbert term is the only operator that breaks three out of four shift-symmetries of the connection, and impose them on the metric-affine Starobinsky term $\alpha R(\Gamma)^2$. This replaces it by $\alpha\mathring{R}^2$, the square of the invariant part of the scalar curvature. The theory propagates only the graviton and one healthy scalar, the metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron. Its potential approaches a plateau polynomially, $U\simeq U_0(1-\mu^2/\chi^2)$, with $\mu=\sqrt{6}\,M_P$ fixed by the curvature of the connection. Once $\alpha\simeq2\times10^{8}$ is set by the scalar amplitude, the model has no free parameters. It predicts $n_s\simeq1-3/(2N_*)$ and $r\simeq2\sqrt3\,N_*^{-3/2}$ at leading order in $N_*$, and $n_s=0.968$--$0.974$ and $r=0.011$-$0.008$ with exact slow-roll for $N_*=50$-$60$ $e$-folds. These values agree with current data, and $r$ is within reach of the next generation of $B$-mode measurements.

candidates.title: Near-Extremal Black-Hole Formation Observed from Null Infinity
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify near-extremal black-hole formation directly from observables at future null infinity. Fully nonlinear evolutions of the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar system in 3+1 dimensions form black holes with charge-to-mass ratios up to 0.993 from regular, horizon-free, superextremal initial data. Quasinormal frequencies and redshift decay independently recover the near-extremal charge-to-mass ratio. Critical mass scaling is recovered at null infinity and charge scaling at the apparent horizon. The charged scalar Newman--Penrose quantity obeys an asymptotic balance law that replaces the conservation law of the neutral theory.
candidates.authors: Thomas M\"adler, Radouane Gannouji, Steven L. Liebling, Emanuel Gallo

candidates.title: Spinors, Doppelg\"angers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelg\"anger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace

candidates.title: Possible detection of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations imprinted in the HI sources from the FASHI catalog
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by curiosity as to whether the observed Universe at low redshifts is well described by the concordance cosmological model, we investigate the large scale angular clustering of extragalactic neutral hydrogen HI sources in the local Universe. Using the second data release of the FAST All Sky HI Survey (FASHI), we analyze a sample of 142,204 HI sources up to $z<0.09$, with a median redshift of $\bar{z} = 0.034$, covering $\sim 40\%$ of the sky. We compute the 2-point angular correlation function, $w(\theta)$, and estimate its covariance using an analytical Gaussian model. We report the possible detection of a broad angular Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) signal, peaking near $50^\circ$. A comparison between a 5th-order polynomial fit and a quadratic baseline yields $\Delta \chi^2 = 9.06$ for $\Delta \mathrm{dof} = 3$ (difference of 3 degrees of freedom), corresponding to a nominal $1.9\,\sigma$ significance for a non-monotonic feature in $w(\theta)$ relative to the monotonic quadratic baseline, although this result alone does not establish a BAO detection. Our analyses show that, due to the projection effect, the expected transverse BAO scale shifts from $64^\circ$ in an infinitesimally thin redshift bin to $52^\circ$ in a bin of thickness $\Delta z = 0.09$, like the data we study, a value close to where our detection peaks, i.e., $\sim 50^\circ$. Furthermore, comparisons with an ensemble of lognormal mocks show that the observed broad bump is consistent with statistical fluctuations at the $1\sigma$ level, meaning that current uncertainties prevent us from unequivocally establishing it as a cosmological signal. Comprehensively, our study establishes a valuable observational baseline for wide-field HI surveys, showing the potential to trace primordial acoustic features even in the low redshift regime, where the transverse BAO signal is dominated by projection effects.
candidates.authors: Felipe Avila, Camila Franco, Armando Bernui

candidates.title: Geodesics in Black-Hole Spacetimes: A Qualitative Classification Using Vieta's Formulae
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.22399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This monograph classifies the geodesics of the Schwarzschild, Kerr and Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes without solving for their turning points. In all three spacetimes, the radial and polar motions are governed by polynomials whose coefficients depend only on the constants of motion, and the qualitative behavior of a geodesic is fixed by the pattern of their roots. We read this pattern directly off the coefficients, using Vieta's formulae together with the discriminant, Descartes' rule of signs, and the values of the polynomials at the horizons and at infinity. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the reciprocals of the radial roots of every non-radial geodesic add up to $1/(2M)$, which gives the third root of a bound orbit in closed form and the separatrix $p=6+2e$. In Kerr spacetime, the signs of the coefficients show that no radially bound orbit has $\varepsilon^2\geq1$ and that vortical geodesics, timelike or null, have no radial turning point; a positive discriminant is necessary but not sufficient for bound motion, and Descartes' rule applied at the event horizon gives the exact criterion. Spherical orbits and their stability, the equatorial ISCO and light rings, and the photon shell follow from the same relations. In Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime, the timelike radial polynomial is a quintic with exactly one negative root, a bound branch requires $\varepsilon^2+\Lambda L^2/3<1$, and both marginally stable circular orbits lie beyond $6M$. Most of these results are known; the aim is to show that a single, elementary algebraic route leads to all of them. The text is meant for graduate students who have taken a first course in general relativity, and each chapter ends with worked examples.

candidates.title: Modeling extreme mass-ratio inspirals in astrophysical and dark-matter environments
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.22480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals offer a powerful probe of massive black holes and their environments, but interpreting their signals requires accurate models of orbital dynamics and radiation. Here we bring together advances in black-hole perturbation theory to establish a unified relativistic framework for adiabatic inspirals in perturbative astrophysical environments. Built on the modified Teukolsky formalism, the framework requires neither post-Newtonian nor slow-rotation approximations. As a first application, we calculate the leading cloud-induced corrections to gravitational-wave fluxes and conservative orbital dynamics for circular, equatorial inspirals around a rotating black hole surrounded by a synchronized ultralight scalar cloud, combining these corrections with the previously calculated scalar response. In our fiducial system, a cloud containing $10^{-4}$ of the black-hole mass produces about $-57.3$ radians of orbital dephasing over two years. The phase contributions from gravitational-wave flux corrections and background-induced orbital shifts each exceed the scalar contribution in magnitude and partially cancel, highlighting the need for coupled matter-gravity modeling. Extensible to other environments and modified gravity theories, our framework provides the relativistic inputs needed to assess detection losses and parameter biases, and to probe the nature of black-hole environments with future space-based gravitational-wave observations.
candidates.authors: Dongjun Li, Hao-Jui Kuan, Colin Weller, Chaoyi Yang, Kelvin Ka-Ho Lam, Patrick Bourg, Adrian Ka-Wai Chung, Yanbei Chen, Nicol\'as Yunes, Huan Yang

candidates.title: Simulating dust collapse: the impact of gauge choices on primordial black hole formation
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate why numerical relativity simulations of dust collapse in a matter-dominated era frequently fail before primordial black hole formation due to numerical limitations and inappropriate gauge choices. Using 3-dimensional fully non-linear simulations of a dust fluid, we detail the advantages of advanced numerical methods and the impact of the lapse and shift evolution equations. The challenge is twofold: 1) conventional lapse slicing evolution equations, highly effective in typical black hole simulations, must be adapted in a cosmological context. We demonstrate how different proposed lapse evolution equations perform, enabling fair comparison, and propose our own. 2) The shift evolution equation's role is to spread out the numerical grid observers for a stable simulation. However, the Gamma-driver evolution fails when confronted with shell-focussing of the dust fluid. We show how the shift damping choice depends on the resolution of the shell-focusing region, suggesting that future work should have spatially varying damping. Our improved gauge choices allow simulations to evolve significantly further and potentially reach black hole formation. The best-performing simulations reach close proximity to a black hole; however, further work on the gauge choice is required for this to be stable.
candidates.authors: Robyn L. Munoz, Christian T. Byrnes, Marco Bruni, Ian Hawke

candidates.title: Primordial Power Spectrum from the Lensed CMB Temperature Spectrum using Iterative Delensing and Fourier Denoising
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.22648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The CMB power spectra are a strong probe of the primordial power spectrum (PPS) of the initial inflationary scalar perturbations. There are many proposed models, from the simpler power law form to various well motivated physical models that predict features in the PPS beyond the power law. Given the large parameter space of possible models, it is necessary to have model independent searches for such features. Weak gravitational lensing alters the CMB temperature power spectrum and can bias free form reconstructions of the primordial power spectrum (PPS) if not accounted for precisely, such as when using estimators like the Richardson-Lucy (RL) deconvolution algorithm. We build on our design of the Non linear Iterative Richardson Lucy (NIRL) estimator that updates the lensing contribution using the freeform PPS recovered at the previous iteration, making it truly model independent in the PPS domain while accounting for lensing. Inspired by signal processing and Fourier filtering techniques from radio interferometry, we also design a Fourier space iterative low pass filter (FLIP) to suppress noise overfitting in NIRL reconstructions. We demonstrate the performance of NIRL-FLIP on a range of simulated PPS models with bootstrap estimates of reconstruction uncertainty obtained from simulated realizations, and show that both our estimator and regularization are robust, accurate and precise, and are able to both reduce lensing induced reconstruction bias and suppress noise overfitting by a significant factor in Fourier space. We provide a detailed description of these results and recommend its utility for future model independent searches for hints of novel physics in the form of deviations from a power law PPS. This can further assist in precise and accurate testing of inflation models, in conjunction with joint cosmological parameter estimation.
candidates.authors: Rajorshi Sushovan Chandra, Debarshi Mukherjee, Tarun Souradeep

candidates.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
candidates.abstract: arXiv:2610.23806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). The halo formation scenario accounts for both observables naturally and without fine-tuning. In the PBH scenario, matching the observed LRD abundance requires a negligibly small PBH mass fraction, and a power-spectrum analysis shows that such a Poisson isocurvature component predicts a clustering signal far below what is observed. The same conclusion holds for any population of dynamically subdominant early-forming seeds, unless their initial clustering is finely tuned or their activity is tied to massive host halos. We conclude that the spatial clustering of JWST LRDs strongly favours the standard halo formation picture and disfavours PBHs, or similar early-forming seeds, as a randomly activated LRD population; PBHs remain viable as seeds only if their activity is governed by massive host halos, in which case clustering alone cannot distinguish them from astrophysical seeds.
